title: The ruler tool answers to a different key on almost every screen
goal: The app binds the Measure tool to the letter I, and one screen of the design study now agrees, but 59 other screens still print M on the same tool. Pick one letter for the ruler and make every screen say it, so someone learning the shortcut from a mock learns the one the app actually uses.
notes: There is a real fork here and it is worth a decision card rather than a guess. Photoshop files its Ruler in the eyedropper group, so both tools are I. docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-gradient-wt.html renders Sample a color (I) and Measure (M) three buttons apart in ONE tstrip, so a blind corpus sweep of M -> I creates a fresh same-bar collision there. Options are (a) Measure takes I everywhere and the eyedropper becomes the shifted sibling in bars that show both, which is the group idiom already written into shared/AGENTS.md and used for Heal J / Patch shift-J, or (b) the eyedropper keeps I and the app moves Measure off I in Sources/PhotonzCore/Tools.swift. Corpus counts today: Measure (M) in 59 pages, Measure (I) in pages/iconography.html only, Sample a color (I) in color.html + icon-gradient-wt.html + shared/colorpicker.js + shared/photonz-ds.js. Detector: node shared/check-shortcuts.mjs from docs/design/mocks.
acceptance: Every screen in the design study prints the same key for the Measure tool
That key is the one Tool.shortcutKey in the app binds, or the app is changed to match and the change is noted
No tool bar ends up with two controls on the same key: node shared/check-shortcuts.mjs still passes
The keyboard legend page shows the final letter

log.note: Review before building. (1) Is I even right? Yes, and no decision card is needed: Tools.swift already binds Measure to i with a written rationale (M is Photoshop's marquee, Photoshop files its ruler under I), shared/AGENTS.md already states 'Measure is I, never M', and pages/lang-keyboard.html already prints I in the legend. The 68 M hints in the corpus are the drift, not the rule. (2) The only real fork the notes flagged: in a bar showing both the ruler and the eyedropper, who keeps the bare letter? Photoshop's I group defaults to the eyedropper, but Photonz has no eyedropper tool at all (Tool has .measure and no sampler; the eyedropper here is a button inside a color popover, and a modal tool in exactly one bar, icon-gradient-wt). Measuring is the product. So Measure keeps bare I and the eyedropper is the shifted sibling, which is the Heal J / Patch shift-J idiom already written into AGENTS.md. Deliberate departure from Photoshop's group default, so it gets written down. (3) Scope call: the eyedropper prints shift-I EVERYWHERE it prints a key, not only in bars where it collides. A key that changes per screen is the exact bug this task exists to kill. (4) Shortest version: sweep the corpus, add the eyedropper to the legend, note the departure in AGENTS.md. The app needs no change.

Shipped. Corpus sweep: 68 Measure key hints across 60 pages went from M to I, in both forms (the button title and the overflow menu keycap). The eyedropper became the shifted sibling on every surface that prints a key for it: tool-strip button and menu row in icon-gradient-wt, menu rows in color and paint, the four color-picker header buttons in color and icon-gradient-wt, the data-tip in comp-color, and the .cp-head sampler in shared/components/colorpicker.js, which is where most pages get theirs. Also gave the sampler ONE name (paint.html said 'Pick color' where every other surface says 'Sample a color') and dropped the now-stale bare 'i' search term from the eyedropper's keywords in shared/icons.mjs. Wrote the inversion down in shared/AGENTS.md so nobody reverses it, and added a Sample a color / shift-I row plus the reasoning to the lang-keyboard legend. Verified: check-shortcuts, check-selection, check-states, check-elevation all pass; all 68 study pages return 200; the DOM of icon-gradient-wt's one shared bar reads Sample a color shift-I next to Measure I in both the buttons and the overflow menu; hovered the eyedropper in a real browser and the tooltip renders 'Sample a color' with a shift-I keycap; Scripts/test.sh 1094 tests pass (no Swift changed).

Review of the built thing. (a) The color-picker sampler now prints shift-I on every page, but that button lives in a popover, not in the tool group, so the keystroke is more a promise than a mechanism. Printing bare I there would have contradicted the ruler on the same screen, so shift-I is the best available answer; flagged in the audit's rough list and as an evaluate question rather than silently accepted. (b) 'Sample a color' wraps to two lines in the legend's Tools column. Pre-existing behavior for long labels (Brush size, Zoom out, Reset overrides all wrap), so left alone. (c) Discovered, out of scope, filed as tool-buttons-in-the-mocks-announce-as-just-butto: tooltip.js's upgrade() moves title into data-tip and deletes the title without setting aria-label, so every tool button in the study announces as a bare 'button'. Confirmed with a Chrome a11y-tree snapshot. (d) No app code changed, so there is nothing to playtest in Photonz Next; the audit says so plainly instead of implying a feature landed.
